name: Runway (Gen-2)
good: Motion brush gives excellent control over what moves. Good consistency.
bad: Heavy watermarking on free tier. Complex motion still morphs terribly.

name: Pika
note: Best for stylized animation and lip sync.
good: Excellent at anime/3D styles. Built-in lip sync is a game changer.
bad: Photorealism lags behind Runway. 3-second default limit is restrictive.

name: Sora (OpenAI)
note: The future, but currently vaporware for most of us.
good: Unprecedented temporal consistency and physics understanding.
bad: Closed beta. Not actually available to use. Known to hallucinate physics on complex interactions.

name: Luma Dream Machine
note: The current best public alternative to Sora.
good: Fast generation. Actually available to the public. Good camera motion.
bad: Heavy artifacting on human faces during movement. Queue times can be brutal.

name: Haiper
good: Excellent short clips. Good at understanding complex textual prompts for motion.
bad: Lacks the fine-grained control (like motion brushes) of Runway.

name: AnimateDiff
good: Total control. Works with existing Stable Diffusion models.
bad: Requires immense technical setup in ComfyUI. Generation takes forever locally.

name: HeyGen
note: The only avatar tool worth using for corporate/talking heads.
good: Flawless lip sync and micro-expressions. Instant avatar cloning.
bad: Not for creative/cinematic video. Strictly for talking heads. Very expensive for volume.

name: Kaiber
note: Best for music videos and audio-reactive generation.
good: Audio reactivity is built-in. Great for trippy, morphing aesthetics.
bad: Terrible at consistency. It's an aesthetic tool, not a storytelling tool.
